mainTopic: How ציצית strings must be made (wound versus loose), which string materials work on which garments, and whether silk garments need ציצית by Torah law
overview: This amud opens with רב and רבה בר בר חנה arguing about a cloak whose ציצית strings were wound all the way down, with nothing hanging loose. רבה בר בר חנה reads the words גדיל and פתיל as a choice, so either style is fine. רב says loose threads are always needed, and גדילים only teaches that four strings are used. Then שמואל, quoting לוי, rules that wool strings work on a linen garment, and the גמרא asks whether linen strings work on wool. רב יהודה answers that both work, and that wool and linen strings work on any garment, even silk. This clashes with רב נחמן, who says silk is exempt; the גמרא explains he means exempt מדאורייתא but obligated מדרבנן, and it works through challenges and proofs from a ברייתא. Using רבא's reading of two פסוקים, wool and linen work for every garment, while other materials work only for their own kind. Finally, the גמרא gives רב נחמן's source from the school of רבי ישמעאל, that a Torah 'garment' means only wool or linen. אביי shows that another teaching of the same school includes silk and other materials.

steps.title: רב and רבה בר בר חנה disagree about a fully wound cloak
steps.stepSummary: The story ends by noting that the ציצית strings were wound all the way down. רב says the cloak is nice but the strings are not. רבה בר בר חנה says both the cloak and the strings are nice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the strings were completely wound up. רב said: The cloak is nice, but the תכלת strings are not nice. רבה בר בר חנה said: The cloak is nice, and the תכלת strings are nice too.
steps.whatsHappening: We finish describing a cloak whose ציצית were wound all the way down with no loose ends. Then two אמוראים give opposite opinions about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the strings are 'not nice' means רב holds they were not made the right way, because nothing was left hanging loose. רבה בר בר חנה holds that ציצית made only of windings are perfectly fine. The rest of the section explains the source of this argument.

keyTerms.meaning: The windings were wound, meaning the strings were wrapped all the way down with nothing hanging loose
Is nice or beautiful, here meaning made properly
A cloak or outer garment
The תכלת (sky-blue) strings of the ציצית, together with the white ones

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody here is criticizing the cloak itself. The whole argument is only about how the ציצית strings were made.

phrases.english: and the windings were wound all the way.
Rav said: The cloak is nice,
but the sky-blue strings are not nice.
Rabba bar bar Chana said:
The cloak is nice, and the sky-blue strings are nice.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: יָאֵי גְּלִימָא וְלָא יָאֵי תְּכֵלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun before this section and presents two opposing opinions about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: ציצית made entirely of windings are not valid in the proper way. רבה בר בר חנה: they are fine.

steps.title: What is the basis of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רב and רבה בר בר חנה are actually arguing about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the root of the argument. This line sets up the next two steps, which give each side's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing who says what is not enough. The גמרא wants to find the source each opinion relies on.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? The standard question asking for the root of an argument

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the two opinions in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle or reading of the פסוקים underlies the argument between רב and רבה בר בר חנה.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה: either wound cords or loose threads
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה points out that one פסוק says גדיל (twisted cord) and another says פתיל (thread). He reads this as a choice: ציצית can be made either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה holds: It is written 'גדיל' and it is written 'פתיל', so it means either wound cords or loose threads.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבה בר בר חנה approved the fully wound strings. Since the תורה uses two different words, either style is acceptable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גדיל means the strings are twisted and wound together. פתיל means a hanging thread. רבה בר בר חנה treats the two words as two acceptable options, so strings that are wound all the way down still count.

keyTerms.meaning: A twisted or wound cord (the windings of the ציצית)
A thread or string hanging loose
Either ... or

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana holds:
It is written 'twisted cords' and it is written 'thread',
phrases.notes: גדילים is in דברים 22:12; פתיל is in במדבר 15:38.

phrases.english: so either twisted cords or a thread.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה סָבַר: כְּתִיב ״גְּדִיל״ וּכְתִיב ״פְּתִיל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 for רבה בר בר חנה's side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two words in the פסוקים give two valid options, so ציצית made only of windings are fine.

steps.title: רב: loose threads are always needed; גדילים teaches the number of strings
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that a loose hanging thread (פתיל) is always required. The word גדילים does not offer an option. It teaches how many strings to use: a singular גדיל would mean two, and the plural גדילים means four. So you make a wound section and let the strings hang loose from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב holds: We really do always need a loose thread. That word 'גדילים' comes to teach a number: a 'cord' means two, 'cords' means four. Make a wound cord and let the threads hang loose from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב's side. He uses the word גדילים for something else, the count of strings, so the requirement of a hanging thread stays in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the two words are not alternatives. Both are required together: part of the strings is wound and part hangs loose. That is why he said the fully wound strings were 'not nice', since they had no hanging part.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, always (insisting on the basic rule)
We require
For counting, to teach a number
And let them hang loose as threads coming out of it

steps.whatToRemember: רבה בר בר חנה: גדיל or פתיל, either one is fine. רב: both together, a wound section with loose threads hanging from it, and גדילים teaches that there are four strings.

phrases.english: And Rav holds: We really always require a thread,
and that word 'twisted cords' comes to teach a number:
a 'twisted cord' means two, 'twisted cords' means four,
make a twisted cord and let the threads hang loose from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב's side, explaining the word גדילים differently from רבה בר בר חנה in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A hanging thread is always required. גדילים teaches that four strings are used, wound together with loose threads hanging from them.

steps.title: Wool strings work on a linen garment
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: שמואל, quoting לוי, rules that wool ציצית strings fulfill the obligation for a linen garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said in the name of לוי: Wool strings exempt a garment made of linen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new ruling about which material the strings may be made of. Wool strings can be put on a linen garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Exempt' means that by attaching wool strings, the owner has done the מצוה of ציצית for the linen garment. The strings do not need to be made of linen to match the garment.

keyTerms.meaning: Wool strings
Exempt, meaning they fulfill the obligation
Linen

phrases.english: Shmuel said in the name of Levi:
Wool strings exempt a garment of linen.
phrases.notes: 'Exempt' here means you have done the מצוה, so the garment has proper ציצית.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּלֵוִי: חוּטֵי צֶמֶר פּוֹטְרִין בְּשֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic, the material of the strings, unrelated to the argument about windings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wool ציצית strings fulfill the מצוה on a linen garment.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new discussion about whether the strings must match the garment's material, which the גמרא goes on to examine.

steps.title: Do linen strings work on a wool garment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether linen ציצית strings fulfill the obligation for a wool garment. It presents two sides: maybe only wool on linen works, or maybe the פסוק allows both directions equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: do linen strings exempt a wool garment? Maybe only wool works on linen, because the תכלת is wool and it works on linen, so white wool works too. But linen on wool would not work. Or maybe, since the Torah puts 'Do not wear שעטנז, wool and linen together' right next to 'Make yourself twisted cords,' there is no difference: wool on linen and linen on wool both work.
steps.whatsHappening: Building on שמואל's ruling that wool strings work on a linen garment, the גמרא asks if the reverse also works: linen strings on a wool garment. It lays out two possible ways to look at it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: wool on linen works only because the תכלת string must be wool, so wool clearly belongs on any garment; linen has no such special status. Side two: the Torah places the ban on שעטנז right next to the command of ציצית. That suggests ציצית permits wool and linen together in any direction.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised: an open question the גמרא tries to settle
Linen
Wool
The sky-blue ציצית string, made of wool
The forbidden mixture of wool and linen in clothing
There is no difference

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן מַהוּ שֶׁיִּפְטְרוּ בְּשֶׁל צֶמֶר?
phrases.english: Do linen strings exempt a wool garment?
It is only wool on a linen garment that exempts,
because since the תכלת exempts [a linen garment],
phrases.notes: The תכלת string is wool, and it clearly works on a linen garment.

phrases.english: white [wool strings] also exempt,
but linen on wool does not.
Or perhaps, since it is written:
"You shall not wear שעטנז,
wool and linen together.
You shall make yourself twisted cords,"
phrases.notes: Putting these two פסוקים side by side hints that ציצית is allowed even with wool and linen mixed.

phrases.english: there is no difference between wool on linen
and linen on wool?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן מַהוּ שֶׁיִּפְטְרוּ בְּשֶׁל צֶמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends שמואל's ruling about wool on linen by asking about the reverse case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether linen strings fulfill ציצית on a wool garment, or whether only wool on linen works.

steps.title: רב יהודה: wool and linen strings work on any garment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רב יהודה's statement: wool works on linen, linen works on wool, and wool or linen strings work on every garment, even silk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רחבה said in the name of רב יהודה: Wool strings exempt a linen garment, and linen strings exempt a wool garment. Wool and linen strings exempt any garment, even silk ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting רב יהודה, who says plainly that linen strings work on a wool garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the question in favor of the second side: the direction does not matter. רב יהודה adds a bigger rule. Wool and linen strings work on garments of any material, even silk.

keyTerms.meaning: In every case: here, on garments of any material
Silk garments

steps.whatToRemember: Wool strings on linen and linen strings on wool both work, and wool or linen strings work on any garment.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as רחבה said that רב יהודה said:
Wool strings exempt a linen garment,
and linen strings exempt a wool garment,

phrases.aramaic: חוּטֵי צֶמֶר וּפִשְׁתִּים פּוֹטְרִין בְּכׇל מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: wool and linen strings exempt in every case,
phrases.notes: "Every case" means a garment made of any material.

phrases.english: and even silk garments.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַחֲבָה אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Linen strings do exempt a wool garment; wool and linen strings work on any garment, even silk.

steps.title: This clashes with רב נחמן: silk is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב יהודה's last point disagrees with רב נחמן, who rules that silk garments are exempt from ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רב נחמן, because רב נחמן said: Silk garments are exempt from ציצית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a conflict: רב יהודה assumes silk garments need ציצית, but רב נחמן says they are exempt. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's words 'even silk' only make sense if a silk garment is obligated. רב נחמן says silk garments have no ציצית obligation at all, so the two disagree on this point.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees
Exempt: not obligated
Strings tied to the corners of a four-cornered garment

phrases.english: And this disagrees with רב נחמן,
phrases.notes: The clash is only about the last part: silk garments.

phrases.english: for רב נחמן said:
Silk garments are exempt from ציצית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Notes that the last clause of רב יהודה's statement conflicts with רב נחמן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: silk garments are exempt from ציצית.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב נחמן from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא cites a ברייתא saying silk garments of several kinds are all obligated in ציצית, which seems to contradict רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב נחמן: A ברייתא teaches that silk, כלך and סריקין garments are all obligated in ציצית.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's ruling with a ברייתא that says silk garments must have ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said silk is exempt. The ברייתא says silk and similar materials are obligated. That looks like a direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of silk material
Another type of silk material
Obligated

phrases.english: רבא challenged רב נחמן:
Silk, כלך, and סריקין garments
phrases.notes: These are all different kinds of silk material.

phrases.english: are all obligated in ציצית

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that silk garments are exempt from ציצית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly says silk garments are obligated in ציצית.

steps.title: The obligation for silk is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means silk garments are obligated מדרבנן, while רב נחמן meant they are exempt מדאורייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן: the ברייתא's obligation is only מדרבנן, so it does not contradict him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one word, the conflict disappears. The ברייתא is talking about a rabbinic obligation, and רב נחמן is talking about Torah law. So silk garments are exempt מדאורייתא, but the חכמים still require ציצית on them.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law
By Torah law
An answer that resolves a challenge

steps.whatToRemember: Silk garments are exempt from ציצית מדאורייתא, according to רב נחמן, but obligated מדרבנן.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying you may wear a silk four-cornered garment without ציצית; he only means the Torah does not require it. The חכמים still do.

phrases.english: By rabbinic law.
phrases.notes: So רב נחמן meant silk is exempt by Torah law, and the ברייתא means it is obligated by rabbinic law.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting levels of obligation: Torah law vs rabbinic law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say silk garments are obligated in ציצית by Torah law, against רב נחמן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers to a rabbinic obligation; רב נחמן's exemption refers to Torah law.

steps.title: Challenge from the end of the ברייתא: wool and linen together
steps.stepSummary: If silk garments need ציצית only מדרבנן, how can the ברייתא allow wool and linen strings on them, which would be כלאים?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the last part of the ברייתא: 'And all of them, wool and linen strings exempt them.' If silk garments need ציצית from the Torah, it makes sense that כלאים is allowed for them. But if it is only מדרבנן, how could כלאים be allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 10, which said silk garments need ציצית only מדרבנן. It points to a later line of the same ברייתא that seems to allow wool and linen strings together on silk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah allows wool and linen together (כלאים) only for a real Torah מצוה of ציצית. A rule that is only מדרבנן cannot override the Torah ban on כלאים. So if the ברייתא allows wool and linen on silk, it seems silk must be obligated מדאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a ברייתא or משנה
Forbidden mixture, here wool and linen together (שעטנז)
'It makes sense if...', which sets up a contrast between two options
From the Torah itself
From the Rabbis

steps.confusionAlert: 'Wool and linen' here does not mean the garment is wool or linen. It means the strings: wool תכלת strings and white linen strings tied together onto the silk garment.

phrases.english: If so, say the last clause:
And all of them, wool and linen exempt them.
It makes sense if you say it is from the Torah:
that is why כלאים are permitted for them,
but if you say it is rabbinic,
how could כלאים be permitted for them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the מדרבנן answer given in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 10 that the ברייתא obligates silk garments only מדרבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows wool and linen strings on silk. כלאים can only be allowed for a Torah-level ציצית obligation, so silk must be obligated מדאורייתא.

steps.title: Read it as wool OR linen
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means either wool or linen strings, not both together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read it this way: either wool or linen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by rereading the line. The ברייתא never meant wool and linen together on silk. It meant you may use either one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the line says 'wool OR linen,' there is no כלאים at all. So the ברייתא no longer proves that silk is obligated מדאורייתא, and the מדרבנן answer from Step 10 survives.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say' or 'read it as'. The גמרא is offering a new reading of a source
Either... or

phrases.english: Say: either wool or linen.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows wool and linen together on silk, which would prove a Torah obligation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא allows either wool or linen alone, so no כלאים is involved.

steps.title: Support: silk strings work only on their own kind
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says silk strings work only for their own kind. That fits a rabbinic obligation, because from the Torah only wool and linen should work.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense, because the last part teaches: 'These exempt their own kind, but do not exempt what is not their kind.' It makes sense if you say it is rabbinic: that is why they exempt their own kind. But if you say it is from the Torah, only wool and linen exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the reading that silk garments are obligated only מדרבנן. It uses another line of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says silk strings can fulfill ציצית on a silk garment. The גמרא assumes that from the Torah only wool and linen strings ever work. So if silk strings work, the obligation must be only מדרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So too it makes sense'. This introduces support for what was just said
Of their own kind, meaning the same material as the garment

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
since the last clause teaches:
they exempt their own kind,
phrases.notes: 'They' are strings made of these silk materials.

phrases.english: what is not their own kind they do not exempt.
It makes sense if you say it is rabbinic:
that is why they are exempted with their own kind,
but if you say it is from the Torah,
it is only wool and linen that exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the מדרבנן answer that Step 12 defended.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא obligates silk garments only מדרבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The last clause of the ברייתא: silk strings work for their own kind only.

steps.title: Rejecting the support with רבא's contradiction
steps.stepSummary: The proof fails. Following רבא, other materials can work for their own kind even from the Torah, because the פסוקים point two ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is because of this, there is no proof. It follows רבא, because רבא pointed out a contradiction: it is written 'the corner', meaning the same kind as the corner, and it is written 'wool and linen'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from Step 13. It sets up רבא's contradiction between two פסוקים, which will show that even מדאורייתא other materials can work for their own kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 assumed that from the Torah only wool and linen strings ever work. רבא shows that one פסוק ('the corner') says the strings should match the garment's material, while another ('wool and linen') points to wool and linen. So same-kind strings might also work מדאורייתא, and the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That is no proof'. The argument does not force the conclusion
Points out a contradiction between two sources
The same kind of material as the corner of the garment

phrases.english: If it is because of this, there is no proof,
in line with רבא, as רבא raised a contradiction:
It is written 'the corner', meaning the kind of the corner,
and it is written 'wool and linen'.
phrases.notes: דברים 22:11, right before the ציצית פסוק in 22:12.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support brought in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from Step 13. It does not prove that silk is obligated מדאורייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 13 assumed only wool and linen work מדאורייתא. רבא's reading allows same-kind strings to work מדאורייתא too.

steps.title: רבא's resolution: wool and linen work for everything, others for their own kind
steps.stepSummary: Wool and linen strings work for any garment. Other materials work only for a garment of the same material.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? Wool and linen exempt both their own kind and other kinds. Other materials exempt their own kind, but do not exempt what is not their own kind.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves his own contradiction by giving each פסוק its own role. This finishes the rejection of the proof from Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Wool and linen' teaches that these two materials work for every garment. 'The corner' teaches that other materials work only on a matching garment. So the ברייתא's rule that silk works for silk fits a Torah obligation just as well, and Step 13 proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'How so?' This introduces how two sources fit together
Other materials besides wool and linen

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, wool and linen strings work on any garment, while other materials work only on a garment of their own kind. Because of this, the line 'silk works for silk' cannot prove that silk garments need ציצית only מדרבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for which ציצית strings may be used on garments of different materials.

phrases.english: How so?
Wool and linen exempt,
whether of their own kind or not of their own kind;
other kinds exempt their own kind,
but do not exempt what is not their own kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבא's contradiction from Step 14 and so completes the rejection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each פסוק is given its own case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים contradict each other: same-kind strings, or only wool and linen.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wool and linen work for every garment. Other materials work only for their own kind.

steps.title: רב נחמן's source: Torah 'garments' are only wool and linen
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן follows the school of רבי ישמעאל. They teach that since the Torah once tells us 'garments' means wool and linen, every unspecified 'garment' in the Torah means wool and linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן holds like the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל. That תנא taught: the Torah usually says 'garments' without saying what they are made of. In one place the פסוק spells out wool and linen. So every 'garment' in the Torah means wool and linen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for רב נחמן's view that silk garments need ציצית only מדרבנן. He relies on a teaching that the Torah's word 'garment' means only wool or linen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method is simple: one פסוק spells out the material, so we use it to explain all the places that don't. If 'garment' always means wool or linen, then the מצוה of ציצית from the Torah applies only to wool or linen garments. Silk garments are then obligated only מדרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Without detail; stated in general terms
Spelled out; specified
Wool and linen
So too, all (the other cases)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how a sage could hold that the Torah obligation of ציצית does not apply to garments of other materials at all.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב נַחְמָן, כִּדְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל.
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman holds like the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael.
As the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Since garments are mentioned in the Torah without detail,
and the verse spelled out for you in one of them
wool and linen,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:47, the פסוק about a garment with צרעת.

phrases.english: so too, all of them mean wool and linen.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן, כִּדְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רבא's reading of the פסוקים, the גמרא now gives the source for רב נחמן's opposite view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every unspecified 'garment' in the Torah means a wool or linen garment, so the Torah's ציצית obligation covers only those.

steps.title: אביי: two teachings from the same school disagree
steps.stepSummary: אביי notes that this teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל goes against another teaching from the same school.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: this תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל disagrees with the other תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי points out a disagreement between two teachings from the same school. This line sets up the next move, where the גמרא quotes the other teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both teachings come from the school of רבי ישמעאל, but they reach opposite results about what counts as a 'garment.' אביי is telling us that רב נחמן's source is only one side of a disagreement, not a view everyone shares.

keyTerms.meaning: Departs from; disagrees with
The other one

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וְהַאי תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
phrases.english: Abaye said: And this tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael

phrases.aramaic: מַפְּקָא מֵאִידַּךְ תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
phrases.english: disagrees with the other tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל מַפְּקָא מֵאִידַּךְ תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the teaching quoted in step 16 and says it is disputed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two teachings from the school of רבי ישמעאל disagree about which materials count as 'garments.'

steps.title: The other teaching: 'או בגד' includes other materials
steps.stepSummary: The second teaching reads 'או בגד' as including garments of camel hair, rabbit wool, goat hair, and kinds of silk, not just wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: from the word 'garment' I would know only a wool garment. Where do we learn to include camel hair, rabbit wool, goat hair, and the silks called כלך, סריקין, and שיראין? The פסוק says 'or a garment.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the other teaching so we can see the disagreement אביי described. This teaching says the Torah's 'garment' includes many materials beyond wool and linen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first teaching (step 16) limits 'garment' to wool and linen. This teaching uses the extra word 'או' ('or') to include other materials, silk among them. So by this view silk is a real Torah 'garment,' which goes against the source רב נחמן relies on.

keyTerms.meaning: I would only know (from this word)
From where do we learn to include?
The verse teaches (by saying)
Hair (here, goat hair)
Different kinds of silk

steps.whatToRemember: There are two teachings from the school of רבי ישמעאל. One says 'garment' means only wool and linen, and רב נחמן follows it. The other uses 'או בגד' to include other materials like silk.
steps.confusionAlert: This teaching is learned from the פסוק about צרעת on garments, not from the ציצית פסוק. The point is what the word 'garment' means in the Torah in general.

phrases.english: As the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"Garment": I would know only a wool garment.
From where do we include camel hair
and rabbit wool and goat hair
and kalakh, serikin and shira'in, from where?
phrases.notes: These three are different kinds of silk.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "Or a garment."
phrases.notes: The extra word 'or' is read as adding more materials.
